sources.title: Spatial Statistics: Lecture Notes
sources.locator: Evgeny Spodarev, complete focused Sections 3.1–3.2, PDF pp. 26–48. Inspected the conditional-expectation prediction argument, simple-kriging Theorems 3.15–3.16, ordinary-kriging Theorem 3.22 and system (3.22), universal constraints (3.28) and system (3.29), Lemma 3.28, and the plug-in and variogram remarks.

contents.name: Section 3.1: conditional expectation as the L2 projection
Theorem 3.2: finite Gaussian-field regression formula and residual-independence proof
contents.reason: The local item proves the conditional-mean claim from zero residual covariance, Gaussian block independence, and conditional-expectation event integrals, without importing stationarity.

contents.name: Theorem 3.15 and equations (3.15)–(3.16): simple-kriging normal equations and weights
Theorem 3.16(i)–(iii): exactness, smoothness, and shrinkage
contents.reason: The assigned theorem proves the optimal weights and error formula; these extra exactness, smoothness, and shrinkage properties need separate statements and hypotheses and are not part of this pair contract.

contents.name: Theorem 3.16(iv): residual orthogonality to the observation span
contents.reason: The local simple-kriging argument uses the affine L2 normal equations that impose zero residual covariance against every observed coordinate; no separate orthogonality theorem is added.

contents.name: Theorem 3.16(v): Gaussian simple-kriging conditional mean
Theorem 3.22 and systems (3.18)–(3.25): ordinary-kriging constrained system and error
Remark 3.23 and Theorem 3.24: intrinsic-field ordinary kriging without finite level moments
contents.reason: This pair's covariance systems require square-integrable field values and do not claim conditional-moment formulas for intrinsically stationary fields lacking finite level moments.

contents.name: Remark 3.25(a): ordinary kriging does not always have the simple-kriging shrinkage property
Universal-kriging constraints (3.28) and augmented system (3.29)
Lemma 3.28: finite-site design rank inferred from orthonormality of trend functions
contents.reason: Orthonormality in a function space does not imply full column rank after restriction to finitely many sites; the local theorem assumes and proves consequences of explicit finite-design full rank.

contents.name: Remark 3.29: estimated covariance and drift introduce plug-in error
Remark 3.30: finite-basis drift estimation and its additional uncertainty
contents.reason: The local definition records that inserting estimated trend values changes the oracle problem; it does not assert an estimation or coverage guarantee.

contents.name: Remark 3.32(a): universal-kriging mean-square error formula
Remark 3.32(b): variogram form of the universal-kriging system
Remark 3.33: additional universal exactness and orthogonality properties
contents.reason: The assigned universal result is the finite-trend unbiased minimum-error system; extra exactness and orthogonality properties are not asserted as separate results.

contents.name: Section 3.1.2: alpha-stable regression results
contents.reason: The assigned covariance-based prediction theorem assumes finite second moments; alpha-stable fields with index below two may not be square-integrable and are a separate prediction theory.

sources.title: Stats 253 Lecture 5: Prediction and Kriging
sources.locator: Dennis Sun, complete Stanford lecture PDF, all 21 pages. Read the correlated-error BLUP derivation on pp. 4–10, model distinctions on p. 17, and variogram discussion on p. 18; remaining historical and graphical slides were inspected as outside the assigned theorem scope.

contents.name: Pages 4–10: correlated-error best linear unbiased prediction and Lagrange system
Page 17: simple, ordinary, and universal kriging model distinctions
Page 18: covariance and variogram formulations
Pages 12–16: kriging history and empirical gold-data figures
contents.reason: The historical narrative and empirical figures do not prove a finite-dimensional covariance or rank claim; the companion page instead verifies exact synthetic finite models.

contents.name: Pages 19–21: fitted empirical variogram curves
contents.reason: The plotted model fits are empirical illustrations and establish no covariance-system invertibility, optimality, or plug-in guarantee used by this pair.
